title: Lemsip Max All in One vs Tesco Health Max Strength All-In-One Capsules

brand.product: Lemsip Max All in One Capsules Cold, Flu, Sore Throat Relief 16s

alternative.product: Tesco Health Max Strength All-In-One Cold & Flu Relief Capsules 16s

summary: Both capsules contain 500mg paracetamol, 100mg guaifenesin and 6.1mg phenylephrine, so the Tesco version is the same all-in-one formula at about a sixth of the price.
evidence: Tesco's Lemsip Max All in One listing states 'Paracetamol 500mg, Phenylephrine Hydrochloride 6.1mg, Guaifenesin 100mg' per capsule, 16 capsules, £7.30. Tesco Health Max Strength All-In-One states 'Each capsule contains the active ingredients: Paracetamol 500mg, Guaifenesin 100mg and Phenylephrine Hydrochloride 6.1mg', 16 capsules, £1.15.
differences: Inactive ingredients and capsule colour may differ. Both rely on oral phenylephrine as the decongestant, whose effectiveness at this dose has been questioned (FDA advisory committee, 2023).

title: Panadol Advance vs Tesco Health Paracetamol 500mg Tablets

brand.product: Panadol Advance 500mg Pain Relief Paracetamol Tablets 16s

alternative.product: Tesco Health Pain Relief Tablets Paracetamol 500mg 16s

summary: Both are 500mg paracetamol tablets taken at the same dose, so the Tesco pack costs about a sixth of the price.
evidence: Tesco's Panadol Advance listing states 'Each Film-Coated Tablet contains Paracetamol 500mg' (16 tablets, £2.15). Tesco Health Paracetamol 500mg is a 16-tablet pack at £0.35 with excipients listed as water, maize starch, pregelatinised starch, povidone, sodium starch glycollate and magnesium stearate.
differences: Panadol Advance is a film-coated tablet that Panadol markets as a faster-dissolving ('Optizorb') formulation; the Tesco listing does not describe a coating. The dose and active are the same.

title: Nurofen vs Tesco Health Ibuprofen 200mg Tablets

brand.product: Nurofen Targeted Pain Relief Tablets Ibuprofen 200mg 16s

alternative.product: Tesco Health Ibuprofen 200mg Pain Relief Tablets 16s

summary: Both are 200mg ibuprofen tablets for pain and fever, so you get the same medicine for a fraction of the price.
evidence: Tesco's Nurofen listing states ibuprofen 200mg per tablet (16 tablets, £1.90). Tesco's own-brand listing is 'Ibuprofen 200mg Tablets' in a 16-tablet pack at £0.35, with an Aldi price-match badge. Same active, same strength, same tablet form and same pack size.
differences: Inactive ingredients differ: the Tesco tablet lists sucrose, talc, titanium dioxide and carnauba wax among its other ingredients, and Nurofen states about 12.7mg sodium per tablet and contains sucrose. Neither difference changes the dose.

title: Gaviscon Heartburn & Indigestion Liquid vs Tesco Health Heartburn & Indigestion Oral Suspension

alternative.product: Tesco Health Heartburn & Indigestion Oral Suspension Aniseed Flavour 500ml

summary: Both are alginate raft liquids with the same three actives (sodium alginate, sodium bicarbonate and calcium carbonate), and the Tesco formula's licence gives the same amounts as Gaviscon's original liquid, at under half the price.
evidence: Tesco's Gaviscon Peppermint 500ml listing states 500mg sodium alginate, 267mg sodium bicarbonate and 160mg calcium carbonate per 10ml (£14.00; Clubcard £12.60 until 10 November 2026). Tesco Health's 500ml aniseed suspension lists sodium bicarbonate, sodium alginate and calcium carbonate (£6.50) but no amounts. The eMC SmPC for Acidex Oral Suspension (Pinewood Laboratories, PL 4917/0027), which names 'Tesco Heartburn & Indigestion relief' among its brand names, gives 250mg sodium alginate, 133.5mg sodium bicarbonate and 80mg calcium carbonate per 5ml, which is the same as Gaviscon per 10ml.
differences: Confidence is medium because the Tesco product page does not print the amounts and the eMC licence that names the Tesco product describes a peppermint suspension, while the Tesco listing checked is aniseed flavour. The flavours differ (peppermint vs aniseed).
